reviews.text:
When you arrive at Bongeunsa Temple, the first thing that catches your eye is Iljumun (一柱門). The gate looks somewhat small compared to the size of the temple. The pillars may look old and plain, but the roof decorations are surprisingly elaborate.

Iljumun is actually a common name for the first gate at the entrance to many Buddhist temples in Korea. When viewed from the side, it looks as if it is supported by a single pillar, so it is also called 'Iljumun Gate'.

reviews.author: Toon Tran
reviews.text:
Revealing the Silent Sentinels: The Profound Beauty of Towers and Monuments
Personally, I am deeply moved every time I encounter these works of art. I remember the moments when I stood in front of historic buildings with traces of time intact. The elaborate carvings on the stupa, which looks like a small pagoda, symbolize enlightenment and serve as a reliquary for the remains and relics of revered monks. The pagoda and monument give a feeling of silence, as if time has stopped. Towers and monuments are not simple structures of stone and cement; they are bridges that lead us to the past and connect us to the unwavering faith of our ancestors.
The monument of merit (tapbi/monument of merit) is no less impressive. These massive stelae, decorated with dragon or turtle motifs, are engraved with eulogies and biographies of prominent figures, especially high-ranking monks, commemorating their virtues and contributions. Although it is written in ancient script, its scale and exquisite craftsmanship speak volumes. I often follow the letters with my eyes and imagine the life and wisdom contained within them. These stelae are powerful evidence of human aspirations and spiritual achievements. These thought-provoking stelae provide a unique window into the richness of Buddhist philosophy and history. Visiting these profound structures is not just a sightseeing tour, but an opportunity for quiet reflection to find calm and inspiration amidst the hustle and bustle of modern life.

reviews.author: Glez. .Romero.
reviews.text:
Bongeunsa Temple was built in the 10th year of King Wonseong of Silla (794).
At the time, it was called Gyeongseongsa Temple and was located near Seongjongneung's Tomb (located at Seonleung Royal Tomb in Seolleung Station), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Standing in the middle of today's luxurious Gangnam, it's hard to believe that just 70 years ago, this area was nothing but farmland and orchards. All the modern facilities we see today were built around Bongeunsa Temple.

reviews.author: Toon Tran
reviews.text:
Embracing the serene embrace of a Buddhist temple, you will encounter images that transcend simple artistry, and you will experience deep contemplation and tranquility. The Maitreya Buddha statue is such a powerful being. Maitreya Buddha, the Buddha of the future, promises a world of hope, joy, and harmony. Maitreya Buddha, depicted with a warm and cozy smile and a round belly, radiates compassion and symbolizes abundance and infinite mercy. Like the majestic Maitreya Buddha statue at Bongeunsa Temple in Seoul, I always feel a sense of quiet optimism whenever I personally encounter these statues. It delivers a powerful message that peace and happiness are always within reach, even in the chaos of life, and that a brighter future is possible if we cultivate kindness and understanding.
Likewise, when you encounter the Lotus Tongeum Bodhisattva statue, you feel this same deep emotional response. Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, or Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, is the Bodhisattva of Compassion, revered for his boundless compassion and ability to hear the suffering of the world. The “pond” in her name symbolizes purity and spiritual growth, like a lotus flower blooming pure from muddy water. When you stand in front of these Buddha statues, you immediately feel comforted and protected. Her calm eyes and gentle posture evoke empathy and inner peace, awakening your own compassion and leading you to discover the quiet strength within yourself. The Maitreya Buddha and Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva statues go beyond simple visual beauty to provide a deeply moving spiritual experience, inviting you to pause, reflect, and enjoy profound moments of tranquility.

reviews.author: Lee Jeong-won
reviews.text:
Capsule Pang is a gacha shop located on the second basement level of Starfield COEX Mall, a representative shopping complex in Samseong-dong.
The term ‘gacha’ in the gacha system is said to be derived from gachapon (ｶﾞチャﾎﾟン), which is used as a synonym for the Japanese capsule toy vending machine gashapon (ｶﾞシャﾎﾟン).
As I mentioned earlier, the popularity of gacha in Korea is truly enormous, and although this type of gacha was originally only available in Japan, it can now be easily found in major cities across the country.

If you head to the second basement level of Starfield COEX Mall, located in the center of Samseong-dong, there is a gacha shop called CAPSULE PANG operating right next to the arcade called FUN CITY.
Capsule Pang tells you to contact Fun City if you have any questions, such as a malfunction when picking up a gacha, so I guess they are probably run by the same company.
Although it is not as large as the large gacha shops that appear recently, the gacha machines are densely packed in a limited space.

A good point is that the gachas currently on sale are displayed so that you can gauge their actual appearance and size.
I also saw some of the gachas I saw during my recent trip to Japan, so they seemed to be constantly changing with new products.

I can’t stop Crayon Shin-chan
When will you come series
Nyanko Great War
spy family
sanrio
Kirby of the Stars
Gundam
Lieutenant Sakeroro
Morph Sand
tom and jerry
Far away
card captor cherry
blue rock
Pokemon

In addition to the list above, there are many gachas with cute and unique characters, so it would be a good idea to visit in person and have fun picking them out one by one.
Please note that it is a system that only accepts card payments, not cash, so you must bring a check or credit card.
At the very back of the store, there is a space with a large mirror and intensive lighting, which is probably a place to take gacha photos or proof shots.
However, it was disappointing that there were so many overlapping gacha devices that it quickly became boring.
I picked up the Dango series from the When to Come series, which I couldn't get as a full set in Japan, but unfortunately, I got a duplicate.

Starfield COEX Mall Capsule Pang, where you can find new gachas in one place.
It seems to be a good place to enjoy gacha for the first time in a while because it has a decent variety of products and plenty of new products.
If you want to pick up a gacha game that is popular these days at COEX, I recommend stopping by at least once.
I have no intention of returning.

reviews.text:
Bongeunsa Temple Bell Tower
Bongeunsa Temple, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, South Korea

The Bongeunsa Temple Bell Tower is a fascinating structure located within the temple grounds and houses symbolic Buddhist tools that mark the monks' daily practice times. Inside the beautiful bell tower, from the left, there is a colorful wooden fish, a large bronze bell, and a large temple bell. These tools play an important role in Buddhist rituals, each representing a different time in the daily routine of meditation and prayer.

Wooden fish, which often symbolize good luck and unity, look like a dragon with a fish tail to me, adding to the mystical atmosphere. The temple bell, a huge bronze bell made with elaborate craftsmanship, clearly displays history, and the beopgo announces the time for meditation with its resonant sound.

Visiting this bell tower not only allows you to admire the beautiful relics, but also gives you a deeper understanding of their role in the lives of Buddhist monks, adding special meaning to your visit to Bongeunsa Temple.

reviews.author: Jo Lee
reviews.text:
This beautiful bell tower features (from left to right) colorful wooden fish, a large bronze bell, and a large temple vault. These are Buddhist instruments that signal the time for monks to perform their daily rituals. Many people say it's a tree fish, but I think it looks like a dragon with a fish tail. I also heard that there was a gong inside the bell tower, but I couldn't really see it.

Each of these instruments has a different meaning.

• The sound of drums saves all living beings on earth.

• The gong is for the rebirth of the public.

• Tree fish are for life in the sea.

• The sound of the bell saves all living beings in the world and underground.

What I especially like are the words engraved on the pillars. These phrases contain blessings and meanings conveyed when playing Buddhist instruments.

聞鐘聲煩惱斷 When you hear the sound of the bell, your worries disappear.
Cultivating wisdom and enlightenment
Leaving Hell and Overcoming the Three Worlds
願成佛島眾生 (Guseong Buddhism Jinsaeng) Do good deeds and save all living beings.

reviews.author: bear sky
reviews.text: Bongeunsa Temple Panjeon is a single-story, gambrel wooden building built in 1856 and renovated in 1878, and is the oldest building within the Bongeunsa Temple grounds. This building is both a Janggyeonggak to store the sutras and a Buddhist shrine to offer worship. It is an architectural rarity, as it has a unique window configuration in order to simultaneously use the functions of storing the sutras and offering worship. The two letters 'Panjeon' are embossed on the signboard that hangs over the eaves of the front eokkan. It is written by Chusa Kim Jeong-hee (his last years of work) and is currently designated as Seoul Metropolitan Government's Tangible Nun Fire No. 83.

reviews.text:
I even reveal my face and leave a review.
I got married at Topaz Hall on June 10th at 12 o'clock.

Since I am a person who plans and produces performances by profession, I negotiated as much as possible with the wedding hall to make the wedding ceremony like a performance, and ended up signing a contract.

After this, due to various problems, we were unable to plan and stage the event, so we proceeded as best as possible according to the conditions of the wedding venue.

However, the biggest problem was that there was no internal communication between the wedding hall staff at all, so the same words were repeated 3-4 times, and no one took responsibility for the miscommunication.

In addition, thanks to the hard preparation by the director and production team, it was a good ceremony even for singers, but many of the guests expressed displeasure at the guidance that seemed to chase them away.

We debated this issue with the person in charge, the manager of the hall, for three hours after the ceremony. Marriage was one of the most important moments in one's life, and there were no measures or manuals for compensation in case such problems arose. In addition, there was no safety manual in a building where more than 400 people gathered on one floor alone, so there was no compensation or countermeasures if a problem occurred, like the Itaewon incident.

The choice is up to you, though.
Even so, I hope you choose the place well for the most important moment of your life that no one takes responsibility for and only avoids.

p.s There is also a recording of this content with the consent of the manager in charge.
